name: Creator campaign performance report
summary: When a creator campaign closes, the marketing lead gets one report built from the store's own orders: what each creator brought in and cost, every creator ranked under a metric set beforehand, and a proposed next step for each. Every number is labelled measured, supplied or estimated.

sources.title: The performance report in Fully Powered AI's own influencer-marketing capability templates (MIT, Fully-Powered-AI/influencer-marketing), rewritten here as a self-contained template that works from files a person supplies: one metric set before the run, every creator ranked, every number labelled measured, supplied or estimated, and a person who decides each creator's next step.

sources.contribution: One metric named in advance decides the order and every creator in the campaign stays in the table; each order is credited once, with any clash between a code and a link kept on record rather than counted twice; and what the figures show is written apart from any guess at why.

A ratio whose divisor is zero or missing is undefined rather than a number, campaign ratios come from summed figures rather than an average of creator ratios, and an arithmetic return is not called profit.
The report opens with what happened and ends with next steps, and the decision itself is left to a person.
Three questions for the next cycle's landing page: whether it matches what the post promised, whether the code is visible, and whether it works on a phone.
Codes and tracked links read together because each catches orders the other misses, and gifted product counted as part of what a creator cost.
The warning that each channel tends to claim the whole sale, which became the check of creator-tracked orders against the store's paid orders from every source.
Profit read beside the sales ratio, a break-even view that became the pays-back reading, and looking for ordinary causes such as stock or tracking before cutting spend.

From its measurement section and its post-campaign checklist: weighing each creator by what a real buyer cost and by whether buyers come back, with reach, likes and media-value figures kept out of the judgement; asking buyers where they first heard of the brand, to catch sales that carry no code; and choosing between a one-off, a repeat and a standing arrangement.
